Both records acknowledge the furniture delivery and the same 230-Bell wage, then give the player a town map. The native Japanese instruction explicitly names R; the English GameCube uses X for the same map action. Change only that approved highlighted button span. Retain the complete English wording, manual lines/pages, pauses, colour count, native actor commands, and map-handoff operation. Ordinary map input and actor traversal remain validation requirements.

Both records are Nook's unfinished-planting-job reminder: open inventory, select seeds or saplings, plant outside, and avoid occupied ground. The native Japanese explicitly uses START; the English reference uses Y for that same inventory action. Normal N64 gameplay confirms START opens inventory and the planting action consumes a supplied seed. Replace only the approved highlighted button span and its length. Retain all GameCube line/page breaks, two pixel-space commands, pauses, colour, and actor commands. The planting reminder itself still requires ordinary actor traversal.

Both records are Nook's reminder to wear the supplied work uniform. The native Japanese explicitly says START opens inventory and A changes clothes after dragging them onto the body. The English reference uses Y to open the same screen. Replace only that highlighted button span, retaining its colour and correcting its length. Keep all GameCube line breaks, page breaks, pauses, other wording, and matching native actor commands. Normal N64 shop progression reaches this record after the uniform handoff.

The Japanese choice explicitly requests editing the message. The legacy adds the noun to its English label; the English GameCube label abbreviates the same action. N64 messages 0382, 0925, 0927, and 0936 reference this choice in the home gyroid menu. Keep those N64 menu IDs and branches: the GameCube gyroid menus expose different actions. This record confirms only this label's identity, not the surrounding dialogue flow or runtime behaviour.

This introductory farewell tells the player that life is more enjoyable with friends and hopes friends will visit the town. The native and English reference commands and actor arguments agree. The legacy text changes the game's English name from Animal Crossing to Animal Forest, which prevents an exact visible-text match but does not change this message's identity. Use the supplied GameCube wording and retain its complete presentation.

The complete native record is identical to native 1091, including all controls. Both are Nook's shop greeting inviting the player to browse. The supplied GameCube 1091 is independently confirmed by the legacy text at 1091, and its English meaning matches this native greeting. Preserve the complete English reference and run the usual command and capacity checks.
